headline: Ponds everywhere
lede: Lemmings-LITE's fourth water stage closed the 'ponds everywhere' gap: open water now sits on all four boards, the drowning is what the east voids say, and the autopilot learned to plug a pond rim with a blocker.

notes.text: #3859 → PR #3861 (1c9488f): THE DOOR and THE LEDGE voids got shores at the walking row, so the punishing east walk ends in the drown — splash, sink, tone — instead of a silent splat; THE SPIRE gained its second pond (a bay east of the exit); THE MASSIF's pace-ground now drowns dawdlers at the west foot.

New rule: a pond rim is an edge. The solver (and every attract replay and autopilot) can now place a blocker at open water — previously its edge test was AIR-only and it could not even see the hazard. The rule is load-bearing on shipped levels: without it THE LEDGE is unwinnable, proven by a hand drift that fired 10 red pins.

lemcheck 191/191 with 13 new pins, --mutate 213/213, lemplay 41/41, a 10/10 browser water drive (both SPIRE bodies paint #2f7fb8, bounces drown on the DOOR shore), gates + build green; prod verified by pixel behaviour, not bundle hash.

Self-audit: the session's own README line about static water read as an open gap to the idle scorer (phantom kick seed, #3074 class) — restated as a DISCLAIMER bullet and shipped same session (#3862), so Lemmings now scores exactly its 3 real gaps: BUILDER, blocker-wake, float-while-dig.

look.text: THE SPIRE from the shore: west pond, and a new bay east of the exit door
FROGGER's ramp now eases at level six before climbing again
